correctness.rationale: Integrating disk slices and twice integrating by parts gives \(u^2F(u,s)/(4\pi)=H(u,s)=\int_0^1g(s(1-x))(1-\cos ux)\,dx\) with \(g(z)=J_0(z)-zJ_1(z)\), transverse \(s=\|\eta\|_2/\alpha\). The Bessel sign estimates make \(g\) strictly decreasing on \([0,2]\), so the continuum of transverse frequencies reduces to \(s=2\). The analytic inequalities prove \(H(u,2)\ge11u^2/120\) for \(0<u\le1\), and \(H(u,2)>1/175\) for \(u\ge14\). For \(1\le u\le14\), a fresh independent exact-Fraction evaluation of the paper-defined degree-40/11-term integrated Taylor polynomial on all 261 nodes found minimum about 0.11520649; its exact rational value exceeds \(1/20\), the uniform Taylor remainder is less than \(10^{-10}\), and the proved derivative interpolation error is at most \(3/80\). This is a complete continuum certificate, not an unsupported finite grid. The zero-axial-frequency original slice integral is positive. Volume \(2\pi/(3\alpha^2)\) and \(j_{3/2,1}<9/2\) give the equal-volume ball comparison at \(\alpha\ge23\). The nonempty closed real zero-set theorem ensures the attained minimum is strictly beyond the closed strip.
